title: Routing ownership sketch for multiregion orchestrator
body:
Purpose:
Sketch to surface a pragmatic ownership split for the control plane components that drive request routing and model execution across regions: API Gateway, Central Orchestrator, Regional Control Planes, and Runtime Adapters. Intended as a lightweight working doc for architecture sync, not a final contract.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus: request routing, traffic steering, failover, and rollout decisions (not infra-level provisioning like k8s autoscaling).
- Regions considered: us-west, us-east, eu-central (initial).
- Two traffic objectives: latency-first (user-facing low-p99) and cost-first (background batch / cheaper instances).
- Runtime adapters encapsulate model runtime specifics (quantization variant, kernel selection).
- We assume an authenticated request reaches the API Gateway; downstream services are internal.

High-level design decisions (quick summary):
1) API Gateway is responsible for initial gating, auth, coarse route classification, and returning a routing token.
2) Central Orchestrator (control-plane brain) owns policy evaluation (customer policies, SLO preferences, rollout state) and produces a routing decision (region + model_variant + runtime_hint).
3) Regional Control Planes own local capacity signals, fast failover, and adaptation within region (e.g., pick a different machine profile or fall back to replica model).
4) Runtime Adapters are owned by serving-runtime but expose a uniform adapter API for the Orchestrator to target. They implement model-specific optimizations and local telemetry.

Ownership map (responsibilities by component):
- API Gateway (team: api-gateway / platform infra):
  - Validate auth, quotas, basic request checks.
  - Classify request into intent buckets (inference, embed, rerank, long-seq).
  - Attach request metadata (customer id, route id, preferred region if provided).
  - Fail fast for syntactic errors or quota exceed.
  - Emit edge telemetry (latency, auth errors).
  - Contract: issue a signed routing token that includes minimal context for the Orchestrator.

- Central Orchestrator (team: platform-orchestration):
  - Evaluate routing policies (customer-configured and system defaults).
  - Maintain rollout state (canaries, percentages, variant pinning).
  - Global decisioning: prefer a region if it meets SLOs and cost constraints; otherwise find fallback.
  - Respond to API Gateway with routing instruction or redirect token.
  - Persist decisions for audit / replay (lightweight event store).
  - Contract: routing API: POST /v1/routing/evaluate -> { decision_id, region, model_variant, runtime_hint, ttl }

- Regional Control Plane (team: regional-runtime-ops):
  - Own fast path reactive decisions: node-level health, eviction, immediate capacity-driven fallbacks within region.
  - Translate orchestration decision to concrete runtime endpoints (adapter URL, pod ID).
  - Local routing for intra-region affinity and cookie-based session stickiness.
  - Circuit-breakers for overloaded model pools.
  - Contract: node-liveness stream, local capacity API, and /resolve endpoint for adapter binding.

- Runtime Adapters (team: serving-runtime):
  - Provide HTTP/gRPC endpoints for model invocation: tokenized request + kv-cache hints + generation config.
  - Implement kernel selection, quantized execution, continuous batching, prefix caching hooks.
  - Emit detailed per-token telemetry (latency, memory pressure, quantization fallback).
  - Accept rollout flags (gradual weights) and expose health / readiness signals.

Routing policy priorities (how decisions are made, highest to lowest):
1) Explicit customer pin (customer has pinned region/model variant)
2) Safety constraints (data residency, compliance)
3) Capacity & SLO compatibility (region must meet p99 latency target given current load)
4) Cost preference (if multiple regions meet SLO, choose cheaper variant/region)
5) Geographic proximity (tie-breaker)

Traffic steering rules (examples):
- Canary model rollout: Central Orchestrator assigns 5% of traffic to variant-v2 in us-west; regional plane to enforce exact percentage locally and report counts.
- Latency-first for interactive customers: Orchestrator will override cost preference and pick lower-latency region even if more expensive.
- Data residency required: Orchestrator filters out non-compliant regions early.
- Burst overflow: if local region capacity < threshold, Regional Control Plane triggers a redirect to Central Orchestrator for cross-region evacuation token.

Failure and degradation modes (who does what):
- API Gateway outage: graceful degrade to maintenance response; no routing decisions possible. Ownership: api-gateway team to escalate.
- Orchestrator partial outage: Regional Control Planes must have a local fallback policy (cached policies + last-known-model-mapping). Orchestrator team owned, but regional ops execute failover.
- Regional plane failure: Orchestrator may route to alternate region if customer permits; runtime-adapter team must ensure model parity.
- Adapter OOMs / kernel errors: adapters expose a soft-fail path (lower-quant model) and report rollup metrics; serving-runtime and regional ops handle mitigation.

Telemetry & observability (who emits what):
- API Gateway: request ingress latency, auth failures, classification rates.
- Orchestrator: decision latency, policy-eval counts, decision_id traces.
- Regional Plane: capacity signals, local failover events, adapter binding latency.
- Runtime Adapters: per-inference latency, memory/GPU metrics, quantization-fallbacks, batch sizes.
- Correlation: all components must carry a trace_id and decision_id to enable end-to-end debug.

SLOs / SLIs to track (minimum set):
- Decision time (Orchestrator) p50/p95/p99 <= 20/100/300 ms
- Binding time (Regional -> Adapter) p95 <= 100 ms
- Adapter inference p99 under configured target (varies by model)
- End-to-end p99 for interactive customers (observed at API Gateway)

Operational handoffs and runbook sketches:
- Canary rollback: if error-rate > threshold for 10m, Orchestrator flag immediately reduces traffic to 0% and notifies owners.
- Cross-region evacuation: Regional plane issues evacuation token and Orchestrator instructs API Gateway to attach reroute header for affected customer ids.
- Emergency scale: escalation path: regional-ops -> infra -> infra on-call. Define phone/Slack runbooks later.

Interface examples (minimal):
- POST /v1/routing/evaluate { customer_id, route, preference: "latency" } -> { decision_id: "d-123", region: "us-west", model_variant: "v2-q8", runtime_hint: "low-latency", ttl: 30s }
- POST /regional/{region}/resolve { decision_id, request_meta } -> { adapter_endpoint: "https://adapter-12.region:443/invoke", bind_token }

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- Do we centralize rollout state in a single Orchestrator cluster (simpler) or replicate to regional planes for HA (more complex but faster failover)?
- How much of policy evaluation should be expressible as a deterministic, cacheable token (to reduce Orchestrator load)?
- Do we permit the API Gateway to short-circuit Orchestrator for a subset of low-risk routes to reduce p99?
- Version negotiation for runtime adapters: should Orchestrator carry adapter-version in decision payload?

Next steps / action items (short-term):
- Priya: draft a compact routing API proto and circulate for review (due 2025-02-09).
- Ethan: run a small simulation of 3-region failover latency/cost tradeoffs using last-quarter traffic mix (due 2025-02-14).
- Marisol: prototype a local policy cache for Regional Control Plane to evaluate outage behavior (POC by 2025-02-28).
- Set an architecture review meeting (platform + serving-runtime + api-gateway) week of 2025-02-03.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Keep the central decision small (decision_id + minimal routing hints). Let regional planes interpret and bind concrete endpoints to avoid global churn.
- Consider an asymmetric caching TTL: short TTL for latency-sensitive classes, longer TTL for background jobs.
- Add a simple numeric compatibility matrix for model parity across regions (later).

References and context: this is intentionally pragmatic and mutable; copy of this will be moved to Confluence after architecture review.

-- end of sketch --
